items.comment: It would be recommended that you mention statistical testing and what statistical tests you use to provide meaningful evidence supporting your results.
items.resolution: New Section 3.5.3 'Statistical testing' in Methods: paired bootstrap CI of differences (10,000 resamples), paired permutation test (model swap; within-model ranks for AUPRC/AUROC, 0/1 decisions for thresholded metrics; DeLong cross-check for AUROC), McNemar's exact test (all rows / mix rows / naive rows), alpha=0.05, Holm adjustment over the seven metrics; script src/router/thesis_stats_tests.py added to Table B.3 (Appendix B.1).

items.comment: I am always skeptical about separating Methods from Implementation since Implementation is your method. So, I would suggest moving the implementation part to the Methods. Now what is absolutely critical to do is that you have a proper Results chapter.

items.highlighted_or_context_text: Section 4.5. ModernBERT achieves higher point estimates than TF-IDF on every aggregate routing-label metric:
items.comment: you cannot make that statement without providing any statistical evidence (as a result of stat testing, some p-value)
items.resolution: The sentence is now followed by the paired statistical evidence (Table 4.2): precision +0.209 [0.115, 0.312], p<0.001 (Holm <0.001); routing-label accuracy +0.078 [0.026, 0.130], p=0.006 (Holm 0.035), McNemar 21 vs 6 (p=0.006); AUPRC/AUROC/balanced accuracy/F1/recall differences not significant (p=0.52/0.165/0.52/0.113/0.127). Versus the type-only heuristic: precision significant (Holm 0.002), accuracy only unadjusted (0.024; Holm 0.096). Per-slice: only compositional precision significant (p=0.003). Claims throughout (abstract, §4.1, §4.4, §5.1, §6.1) restated accordingly; §5.6.5 gives minimum detectable differences.

items.comment: This discussion of the results reflects their analysis and interpretation. It should be integrated with the Results. You present the results, explain them, analyse and interpret. Here you present all the results and then you discuss all the results. These aspects should be inherently intertwined - finding after finding. Also, the analysis has to be supported by statistical testing to provide statistically meaningful evidence. Otherwise everything is inconclusive, reflecting trends rather than concrete conclusive outcomes.
items.resolution: Old §4.5 Discussion dissolved into the Results chapter: each finding is presented, explained and interpreted in place (§4.1 classification + tests, §4.2 cost and error types + McNemar, §4.3 thresholds/frontier, §4.4 per-type + per-slice tests, §4.5 answer-quality retention, §4.6 seed stability). Statistical support added where claims are made.
